pos.personaBrief: Dortmund and Chelsea built through central midfielders with emphasis on possession and control, but he adapted by opponent and Bundesliga.com notes he often defends deeper rather than counter-presses.

pro.personaBrief: His signature is playing out through central midfielders and a 3-2 build-up that invited pressure, with line-breaking playmakers like Weigl and Gundogan.

est.personaBrief: Positional structures (3-2-5, 2-3-5) with demanded rotations of central players and lenient problem-solving; attackers drift between half-spaces.

lar.personaBrief: Chelsea were narrow in possession, relying on central areas and half-spaces, with wing-backs and full-backs the only wide players and wingers not essential.

blo.personaBrief: Mixed: energetic man-oriented press at Dortmund and wing-back triggered press at Chelsea, but a deep 5-3-2 and a tendency to structure defensively after losing the ball.

mar.personaBrief: Chelsea pressed zonally with triggers and spaces covered, though Dortmund had man-oriented midfield pressing and a tailored plan against Bayern.

pla.personaBrief: Bundesliga.com and Mastermind stress he varies plans for each opponent and even changes shape at half-time, shaped around available players.

res.personaBrief: Pragmatic: deep 5-3-2 away to Bayern, extra defenders to close games, defensive set-piece focus, and a Champions League winner built on stability.

sis.personaBrief: Strong tactical system with defined duties for all, though he gives players some freedom to problem-solve; frictions with stars like Kimmich show role demands over license.

jog.personaBrief: Prefers technically capable central midfielders who pass and rotate (Weigl, Gundogan, Kante and Kovacic double six) with intensity demanded, little room for a non-running 10.

bas.personaBrief: Built around established stars and signings (Kane, Kimmich, Chelsea veterans); little evidence of academy-first policy.

lid.personaBrief: Demanding, publicly critical of his squad, clashes with Kimmich and the dressing room at Bayern, exits from Dortmund and Bayern; authority over harmony.
